quarterly_data.signal: Duke Energy Progress' 2025 North Carolina rate case: on August 5, 2026 it filed a Comprehensive Revenue Requirement Settlement with the Public Staff and other intervenors resolving all revenue requirement issues - a 9.8% ROE with a 53% equity component, a North Carolina retail rate base of approximately $17.8 billion for the historic base case, and approximately $3.4 billion of capital (NC retail allocation) projected to go in service over the 2-year multi-year rate plan, with an annual MYRP refund mechanism. The settlement results in a revised revenue requirement increase of $338 million over the two-year period, an average annual rate increase of 3.4% over two years (the initial filing requested approximately $729 million); DEP will increase the flow back of production tax credits to customers to $120 million annually for 2027 and 2028 (from $40 million annually in its original request). The parties agree to support a separate proceeding to evaluate a large load tariff, intended to be completed before new rates take effect; DEP will evaluate delaying its next base rate case filing until no earlier than November 1, 2028 if permitted to defer costs of the Commission-approved Person County CC1 and Marshall CTs. Subject to NCUC approval (evidentiary hearing scheduled to begin August 11, 2026); DEP has requested Year 1 rates to be in effect no later than January 1, 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: 9.8% ROE; rate base approximately $17.8 billion; MYRP capital approximately $3.4 billion; revenue requirement increase $338 million over two years
